subject: Information Theory
title: RSA Encryption
description: Learn RSA Encryption in one minute.

hook.text: Multiply two huge primes: easy. Factor the result back into those primes: extraordinarily hard. RSA lives in that gap.

buildup.text: Rivest, Shamir, and Adleman published RSA in 1977. It uses two keys: public for encryption, private for decryption.

discovery.text: Anyone can encrypt with your public key. Only you can decrypt with your private key. Key sharing is solved.

twist.text: RSA is slow compared to symmetric ciphers. In practice, RSA encrypts a symmetric key, which encrypts the data.

climax.text: Every HTTPS connection uses this hybrid: RSA for key exchange, AES for bulk encryption.

punchline.text: Two keys. One public, one private. Problem solved.

quiz.question: What mathematical problem makes RSA secure?
options: Factoring the product of two large primes
